title: Order the time machine
prompt:
The time machine's cards fell on the floor. Write `in_order(events)`, which returns a new list sorted oldest first and leaves the original alone, and `span(events)`, the number of years from the oldest event to the newest.

When it works, `python3 timeline.py` starts with 1958 and ends with `span: 59 years`.
expected_output:
1958 Rosenblatt's perceptron article
1959 Samuel's checkers paper
1986 backpropagation becomes widespread
2017 transformer architecture
span: 59 years
hints: `sorted(...)` makes a new list; `.sort()` changes the old one. Which one does the test want?
Tuples sort by their first item, so `sorted(events)` already sorts by year.
For `span`, collect the years into a list and subtract `min` from `max`.
explain_after: Every event on this list comes from a cited source. Rosenblatt's perceptron article appeared in Psychological Review in 1958 [ml-098]. Samuel's 1959 paper reports a checkers program that learned to play better than its programmer [ml-097]. Training by error backpropagation became widespread with Rumelhart et al. in 1986 [ml-093], and Jurafsky and Martin date the transformer to 2017 [ml-092].
